holidays.name: National Acorn Squash Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the humble, ridged, dark-green winter squash. Celebrate by roasting it with butter and brown sugar, stuffing it with sausage and apples, or just admiring its acorn-like shape.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it is an unofficial observance that grew out of food-themed calendars and social media. It lands in early September, when winter squash starts arriving at markets.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, acorn squash is a winter squash, but it is a type of summer squash species, Cucurbita pepo. It is named for its shape, not for any relation to oak trees.

holidays.name: National Beer Lover's Day
holidays.description: A day for people who love beer to raise a glass of their favorite brew, whether it is a crisp lager, a hoppy IPA, or a dark stout. Breweries and bars often offer specials.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial American observance, popular with brewers and bar owners as a way to celebrate beer culture, especially as craft brewing has grown.
holidays.funFact: Beer is among the oldest fermented beverages in the world, with evidence of brewing going back more than 5,000 years in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt.

holidays.name: Neither Snow nor Rain Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the dedication of postal workers, inspired by the famous unofficial motto about carriers not being stopped by bad weather. Send a letter or thank your mail carrier.
holidays.origin: The phrase comes from an inscription on the James Farley Post Office in New York City, which is not an official US Postal Service motto. It was adapted from the writings of Herodotus about ancient Persian couriers.
holidays.funFact: The famous line was written by Herodotus about the Persian mounted couriers in the 5th century BC, long before the modern postal service existed.

holidays.name: Brazil Independence Day
holidays.description: Known as Sete de Setembro, Brazil celebrates its independence from Portugal with parades, military displays, and patriotic festivities across the country.
holidays.origin: On September 7, 1822, Prince Pedro, later Emperor Pedro I, declared Brazil independent from Portugal near the Ipiranga River in the famous Cry of Ipiranga.
holidays.funFact: The independence proclamation was made by a future emperor, so Brazil became an empire first and did not become a republic until 1889.

holidays.name: National Salami Day
holidays.description: A cured-meat celebration where fans of salami gather to enjoy slices on charcuterie boards, sandwiches, and pizzas.
holidays.origin: This unofficial food holiday comes from food-holiday calendars, which promote the many kinds of salami from Italy, Hungary, Germany, and elsewhere.
holidays.funFact: The word salami comes from the Italian word salame, which traces back to the Latin sal, meaning salt, the main preservative used to cure it.
